To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hypofractionated radiation therapy is a safe and effective adjuvant treatment for melanoma.

(1) hypofractionation (HF) for adjuvant radiotherapy (RT) in melanoma is safe and effective, with a comparable local control rate to that of conventional fractionation (CF), (2) HF is associated with a significantly lower rate of grade ≥3 late toxicities compared to CF, (3) HF for adjuvant RT is cost-effective compared with CF.

(i) hypofractionated radiotherapy (HFXRT) is as effective as conventional fractionated radiotherapy (CFRT) in the adjuvant management of high risk cutaneous melanoma; (ii) HFXRT is associated with a lower rate of grade ≥2 acute toxicity; (iii) HFXRT may be associated with a higher rate of late toxicity, but this needs further study.
